Subject: QuietRidge on-prem deployment: initial checklist and constraints

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at QuietRidge is excited to proceed with an on-prem/private deployment. We have a few initial constraints to share so your architecture team can advise:

- Target cluster: 3 AZ-equivalent racks in our Mountain View colo (single DC).
- GPUs: We plan to start with 2 x A100-40GB per rack, may scale to 4 per rack in Q3.
- Storage: primary model store on NVMe-backed block storage (fast), and an archive tier on network-attached HDDs.
- Network: private VPC with reserved public egress via a firewall appliance; strict egress rules for telemetry.
- Compliance: we need SOC2-aligned audit logs and KMS-integration (customer-managed keys).

Before we lock dates, can you send a quick preflight checklist and call out anything that will block a non-disruptive handoff to our operations team? Also curious how Redwood recommends node pool sizing for mixed GPU/CPU workloads and any preferred CSI drivers for the NVMe layer.

Appreciate it — we can take a short sync on Mon if helpful.

—Sam

Hi Sam — great to hear. Short answer: nothing obvious blocking, but a few clarifying asks and a preflight checklist attached. High-level notes below, then Karthik will add the technical sizing guidance.

Quick clarifications (we'll confirm on the call):
- Single-DC with 3 racks is fine; we treat them as failure domains for nodepool placement.
- For GPU scaling, we recommend reserving headroom in the dedicated pool (we'll propose an autoscale band in the SOW).
- On telemetry: we can minimize egress by routing metrics and traces through a private collector; we can supply a containerized collector to run in your VPC.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations; we will include key-rotation steps in the onboarding playbook.

I attached: redwood_preflight_checklist_v1.pdf, a simple network diagram, and a draft SOW template to speed contracting.

Next steps: 1) Karthik to propose nodepool/storage sizes and CSI recommendation; 2) Ops checklist confirmation from QuietRidge; 3) schedule an implementation kick on Wed 2/25 if both sides are ready.

On Sat, Feb 22, 2026 at 11:02 AM marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sam — great to hear. Short answer: nothing obvious blocking, but a few clarifying asks and a preflight checklist attached.

Sam / Priya — adding the technical recommendations so you have a concrete starting point. TL;DR: two GPU nodepools (prod-gpu, batch-gpu), one cpu-only nodepool for system services + lightweight workloads; NVMe via hostPath-provisioned CRI-friendly CSI (we prefer vendor-provided NVMe CSI or LVM-on-NVMe with CSI driver). Detailed suggestions below.

1) Cluster topology
- Control plane: managed by QuietRidge (you) — we recommend 3 dedicated control-plane nodes on a separate VLAN or out-of-band management network.
- Worker nodepools:
  - prod-gpu: 6 nodes initially (2 A100/40GB per node), tuned for low-latency serving, isolated taints: redwood/serving=true:NoSchedule.
  - batch-gpu: 4 nodes, larger batch sizes allowed, lower priority preemption; can be spot-equivalent if you use preemptible pricing.
  - infra-cpu: 3-4 m6i-equivalent nodes for logging, monitoring, collectors, build agents.

2) Storage
- Hot store (models + KV caches): local NVMe per GPU node. Use a CSI that supports topology-aware volume provisioning so pods co-locate with NVMe. Suggest using the vendor NVMe CSI or LVM+CSI for snapshot support.
- Medium-term store: distributed block (Ceph/Rook or external SAN) mounted with RWX where shared model artifacts are needed.
- Archive tier: object store reachable over internal network (S3-compatible gateway to on-prem archive).
- Backups & snapshots: daily model snapshot to archive, weekly full; ensure storage class supports snapshots and retention labeling.

3) Networking & egress controls
- Recommend enforcing egress via an internal NAT + firewall appliance; allow only specific telemetry endpoints.
- Ensure MTU and jumbo-frame consistency across racks for high-throughput model pulls.
- Plan B for large model downloads: pre-stage images/weights to a nearby artifact registry on the same DC to avoid cross-rack egress.

4) Observability & compliance
- Audit logs: enable cloud/audit-level logging at API server and persist to your archive with SOC2 retention window.
- KMS: use your HSM gateway; Redwood will integrate during onboarding.

4) CSI recommendation summary
- If you have a vendor NVMe stack (e.g., Pure, NetApp with NVMe-oF), use vendor CSI.
- Otherwise LVM-on-NVMe + open-source CSI (e.g., csi-lvm) with snapshot support.

I'll sketch an initial node-sizing doc and share by Monday morning. Flagging two likely friction points: (1) KMS/networking approvals can take 2–3 weeks in procurement; (2) vendor CSI drivers may need kernel compatibility checks on your host OS images.

-Karthik
